title: Integrated Nutrient Management (INM) & Rational Fertilizer Usage Guidelines
source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Soil Science (IISS), Bhopal
content: Integrated Nutrient Management combines inorganic chemical fertilizers with organic manures, bio-fertilizers, and green manuring. The 4R Nutrient Stewardship principle: 1. Right Source, 2. Right Rate, 3. Right Time, 4. Right Place. Urea Management: Use 100% Neem-Coated Urea (NCU). Neem coating slows down nitrification and reduces volatilization losses by 15-20%. Never broadcast urea on dry soil under bright sun. Deep placement (5-7 cm below seed) or incorporation into moist soil increases Nitrogen Use Efficiency (NUE) from 30% to over 50%. Phosphorus management: Apply DAP (Di-ammonium Phosphate) or SSP (Single Super Phosphate) basally. SSP also supplies 11% Sulphur and 19% Calcium, making it superior for oilseeds and pulses. Potassium management: MOP (Muriate of Potash, 60% K2O) should be applied in splits in sandy soils to prevent leaching. Biofertilizers: Seed inoculation with Azotobacter/Azospirillum (N-fixers) and PSB (Phosphate Solubilizing Bacteria - Bacillus megaterium) saves 20-25 kg chemical N and P2O5 per hectare.
